turns.query: Our ORP reads 60 mV lower than the pod across the bay. Which one is wrong?

relevant.evidence:
ORP reference offset: ORP values depend on the electrode’s reference type (Ag/AgCl vs.
standard hydrogen electrode). Record which reference is used so values are comparable across
DataPods and over time. Treat ORP trend as more reliable than absolute value.

An ORP probe has a platinum tip that is connected to a silver wire, surrounded by
silver chloride. That silver wire is then connected to a KCL reference solution.

Seawater’s high ionic strength makes absolute
readings less comparable between sites — trend matters more than the raw number.

turns.query: So what should I compare instead?
turns.noRelevantChunks: Pure-deixis follow-up: the raw turn names nothing to compare. Unanswerable in isolation — retrieval runs on this text alone (gate ◆G11).
